explanation_text:
This employee is classified as LOW RISK of attrition (probability: 53.9%).

Note: feature contributions below are SHAP values in model score space, not direct probability percentage points.

The primary contributing factor is training hours (-1.48), with SHAP impact 1.235 score units. Additionally, work hours per week (1.48) and work life balance (-1.56) further elevate the risk with SHAP impacts 0.610 and 0.116 respectively.

Positive factors such as promotions (0.51) and tenure performance (ratio) (-0.25) help reduce the overall risk (SHAP impacts -0.751 and -0.260 respectively).

rule_recommendations.action: Increase annual training allocation by a minimum of 20 hours. Enrol the employee in a structured learning pathway aligned to their career goals (e.g., technical certifications, leadership development programmes).
rule_recommendations.evidence: Organisations investing in employee L&D report 24% higher retention rates (LinkedIn Learning, 2023; Noe, 2020).

rule_recommendations.action: Review total contracted and actual hours. Reduce excess hours via task prioritisation frameworks (e.g., MoSCoW) or additional team resource allocation.
rule_recommendations.evidence: Consistently high weekly hours degrade cognitive performance and decision-making quality, accelerating disengagement and eventual departure (Pencavel, 2015).

rule_recommendations.action: Implement hybrid or remote work options. Enforce 'right to disconnect' policies outside contracted hours. Offer additional leave days or mental health days.
rule_recommendations.evidence: Poor work-life balance is consistently ranked as one of the top three reasons for voluntary resignation in HR surveys (SHRM, 2023; Gallup, 2022).

rule_recommendations.action: Conduct a workload audit across the team. Redistribute projects, defer non-urgent tasks, and set explicit boundaries on concurrent project assignments.
rule_recommendations.evidence: Composite workload intensity is a robust predictor of intention-to-leave (Spector & Jex, 1998; Maslach et al., 2001).

rule_recommendations.action: Increase the annualised training rate. Review if learning opportunities are being offered equitably and whether the employee has had access to relevant upskilling pathways.
rule_recommendations.evidence: Low training-per-year ratios signal neglect of career development, a key engagement driver (Saks, 2006).
